15-2.solution: The quarterly rate \(q\) must satisfy \((1 + q)^4 = 1.12\), so \(q = 1.12^{1/4} - 1 \approx 2.87\%\). Splitting \(12\%\) into \(3\%\) a quarter would give \(1.03^4 = 1.1255\), more than \(12\%\) a year.

15-20.solution: Doubling in 6 years is 24 quarters: \((1 + q)^{24} = 2\), so \(q = 2^{1/24} - 1 \approx 2.93\%\).

15-22.solution: With semi-annual compounding at nominal rate \(j\): \(\left(1 + \frac{j}{2}\right)^2 = 1.16\), so \(\frac{j}{2} = \sqrt{1.16} - 1 = 0.07703\) and \(j \approx 15.41\%\).
